topics.title: Rhythmic Pattern: Meaning of Rhythm, Types of Rhythm, and Bass Drum Rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 2 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
RHYTHMIC PATTERN: MEANING AND TYPES OF RHYTHM, AND BASS DRUM OF NIGERIAN THE NATIONAL ANTHEM
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Introduction to Life Drawing: Meaning, Importance, Parts of the Human Body, and Sketching a Full Human Figure | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 1 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - RHYTHMIC PATTERN
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Rhythm
3. Bass Drum Rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem
4. Importance and Materials for Learning Rhythm
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of rhythm.
2. Identify the types of rhythm.
3. Explain the importance of rhythm in music.
4. Identify the bass drum and describe its use.
5. Demonstrate the bass drum rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem through clapping or drumming.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about music notes and their values, solfa notation, and rhythmic patterns.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the types of rhythm and the bass drum rhythm used in the Nigerian National Anthem.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Bass drum
2. Drumsticks
3. Tambourine
4. Clap sticks
5. Metronome (if available)
6. Audio recording of the Nigerian National Anthem
7. Charts showing rhythmic patterns
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
When we sing the Nigerian National Anthem, everyone follows the same steady beat. That steady beat is called rhythm. Musical instruments, especially the bass drum, help to keep this rhythm so that singers and instrumentalists perform together correctly.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of rhythm, the types of rhythm, and how the bass drum is used to maintain the rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF RHYTHM
Rhythm is the regular pattern of beats or sounds in music. It is the movement of music through time and helps to keep the music steady.
TYPES OF RHYTHM
The common types of rhythm include:
1. Simple rhythm - A regular and easy pattern of beats.
2. Complex rhythm - A combination of different beat patterns.
3. Fast rhythm - A rhythm played at a quick speed.
4. Slow rhythm - A rhythm played at a gentle speed.
BASS DRUM
A bass drum is a large percussion instrument that produces deep, low sounds. It is used to keep the main beat in a musical performance or marching band.
BASS DRUM RHYTHM OF THE NIGERIAN NATIONAL ANTHEM
The bass drum helps to maintain the steady beat while the Nigerian National Anthem is being sung or played.
The bass drum player should:
1. Keep a steady beat.
2. Follow the conductor or band leader.
3. Strike the drum evenly.
4. Play in time with other instruments.
5. Avoid playing too loudly or too softly.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF RHYTHM
Rhythm helps to:
1. Keep music organised.
2. Help singers and instrumentalists stay together.
3. Make music enjoyable.
4. Improve coordination and concentration.
5. Support dancing and marching activities.
MATERIALS FOR LEARNING RHYTHM
1. Bass drum
2. Drumsticks
3. Metronome (if available)
4. Tambourine
5. Clap sticks
6. Audio recording of the Nigerian National Anthem
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Rhythm is the regular pattern of _______ in music.
A. pictures
B. colours
C. beats
D. letters
2. Which musical instrument produces a deep, low sound?
A. Bass drum
B. Flute
C. Recorder
D. Whistle
3. Which of the following is a type of rhythm?
A. Wooden rhythm
B. Simple rhythm
C. Plastic rhythm
D. Paper rhythm
4. The bass drum helps to _______.
A. paint fabrics
C. write stories
D. keep a steady beat
5. The Nigerian National Anthem should be played with _______.
A. no rhythm
B. a steady rhythm
C. random beats
D. very loud noise only
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: beats, rhythm, simple, anthem, bass drum
6. _______ is the regular pattern of sounds in music.
7. A _______ produces deep, low sounds.
8. Rhythm is made up of regular _______.
9. _______ rhythm is easy to follow.
10..The Nigerian National _______ is sung with a steady rhythm.
C. True or False
11. Rhythm helps to keep music organised. _______
12. The bass drum is a percussion instrument. _______
13. Fast rhythm is played slowly. _______
14. The bass drum helps singers keep the correct beat. _______
15. Clapping can be used to practise rhythm. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B
Column A - Column B
16. Rhythm - A. Used to play the drum
17. Bass drum - B. Deep, low sound
18. Nigerian National Anthem - C. Regular pattern of beats
19. Simple rhythm - D. Patriotic song
20. Drumstick - E. Easy beat pattern
ANSWER KEYS
1. C - Beats
2. A - Bass drum
3. B - Simple rhythm
4. D - Keep a steady beat
5. B - A steady rhythm
6. rhythm
7. bass drum
8. beats
9. simple
10. anthem
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. C - Regular pattern of beats
17. B - Deep, low sound
18. D - Patriotic song
19. E - Easy beat pattern
20. A - Used to play the drum
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that rhythm is the regular pattern of beats or sounds in music that helps to keep music steady and organised.
Pupils identified the types of rhythm, which include simple rhythm, complex rhythm, fast rhythm, and slow rhythm. They also learned that rhythm is important because it helps singers and instrumentalists perform together, improves coordination and concentration, and makes music enjoyable.
Furthermore, pupils learned that the bass drum is a large percussion instrument that produces deep, low sounds and is used to maintain the main beat during musical performances.
Finally, pupils practised the bass drum rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem through clapping and drumming activities, and understood the importance of keeping a steady beat while singing or playing the anthem.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher plays or sings the Nigerian National Anthem and asks pupils to clap along with the steady beat. The teacher introduces the concept of rhythm.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen carefully, clap to the beat, and respond to the teacher’s questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Rhythm - The teacher explains that rhythm is the regular pattern of beats or sounds in music that keeps music moving steadily.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of rhythm in their own words.
Step 3: Types of Rhythm - The teacher explains the common types of rhythm:
- Simple rhythm
- Complex rhythm
- Fast rhythm
- Slow rhythm
The teacher demonstrates each type by clapping or tapping different beat patterns.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils clap and identify the different rhythmic patterns demonstrated.
Step 4: Bass Drum and Its Use - The teacher displays a bass drum (or a picture of one) and explains that it is a percussion instrument used to maintain the steady beat in music. The teacher also, demonstrates the bass drum rhythm used while performing the Nigerian National Anthem.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the demonstration and identify the role of the bass drum.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher guides pupils to clap, tap, or play simple rhythmic patterns while singing the Nigerian National Anthem.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils practise keeping a steady rhythm through clapping, tapping, or drumming.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of rhythm.
- Group 2: Identify and explain the types of rhythm.
- Group 3: State the importance of rhythm in music.
- Group 4: Demonstrate the bass drum rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem through clapping or drumming.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, practise, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning of rhythm, the types of rhythm, the importance of rhythm, and the role of the bass drum in maintaining the beat of the Nigerian National Anthem.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils as they demonstrate rhythmic patterns through clapping or using percussion instruments.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate simple rhythmic patterns confidently.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Theatrical Elements and Personnel: Elements of a Play Production, Theatre Personnel, and Notable Nigerian Theatre Practitioners | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 3 Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of rhythm.
2. Identify the types of rhythm.
3. State at least three importance of rhythm in music.
4. Identify the bass drum and explain its use in musical performances.
5. Demonstrate the bass drum rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem through clapping, tapping, or drumming.
6. Keep a steady beat while singing or listening to the Nigerian National Anthem.

topics.title: Theatrical Elements and Personnel: Elements of a Play Production, Theatre Personnel, and Notable Nigerian Theatre Practitioners | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 3 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
THEATRICAL ELEMENTS AND PERSONNEL: ELEMENTS OF A PLAY PRODUCTION, THEATRE PERSONNEL AND NOTABLE NIGERIAN THEATRE PRACTITIONERS
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 3
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Rhythmic Pattern: Meaning of Rhythm, Types of Rhythm, and Bass Drum Rhythm of the Nigerian National Anthem | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 2 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - THEATRICAL ELEMENTS AND PERSONNEL
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Elements of a Play Production
3. Meaning and Importance of Theatre Personnel, and Notable Nigerian Theatre Practitioners
4. Materials used in a Play Production
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of a play production.
2. Identify the elements of a play production.
3. Mention the different theatre personnel and state their duties.
4. Identify some notable Nigerian theatre practitioners.
5. State the contributions of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners to the development of theatre in Nigeria.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about drama and theatre, acting, impersonation, and character development.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the elements of a play production, the people involved in producing a play, and famous Nigerian theatre practitioners.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Drama script
2. Pictures or charts showing a stage and theatre personnel
3. Samples of costumes and stage props
4. Pictures of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners
5. Flashcards showing different theatre personnel and their duties
6. Multimedia projector (if available)
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Whenever a drama is performed on stage, many people work together to make the performance successful. Besides the actors and actresses, there are directors, producers, costume designers, stage managers, and other theatre personnel who help in preparing the play. Nigeria also has many famous theatre practitioners who have contributed greatly to the growth of drama and theatre.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the elements of a play production, the duties of theatre personnel, and some notable Nigerian theatre practitioners and their contributions.
LESSON 1 - ELEMENTS OF A PLAY PRODUCTION
A play production is the process of preparing and presenting a drama before an audience.
The major elements of a play production include:
1. Script - The written story or dialogue.
2. Actors and Actresses - People who perform the roles.
3. Stage - The place where the drama is performed.
4. Costumes - Clothes worn by the actors.
5. Props - Objects used during the performance.
6. Lighting - Lights used to improve visibility and create effects.
7. Sound and Music - Music and sound effects used during the performance.
8. Audience - People who watch the play.
THEATRE PERSONNEL AND THEIR DUTIES
Theatre personnel are the people who work together to produce a successful play.
1. Producer - Organises and finances the play.
2. Director - Guides and supervises the actors and the production.
3. Actor/Actress - Performs different roles in the play.
4. Stage Manager - Coordinates activities on the stage.
4. Costume Designer - Designs and prepares costumes.
5. Make-up Artist - Applies make-up to actors.
6. Lighting Technician - Operates the stage lights.
7. Sound Technician - Controls music and sound effects.
8. Prop Manager - Prepares and manages stage properties.
LESSON 2 - NOTABLE NIGERIAN THEATRE PRACTITIONERS
Some famous Nigerian theatre practitioners include:
1. Hubert Ogunde - Hubert Ogunde (1916-1990) was a Nigerian playwright, actor, musician, and producer. He is widely regarded as the father of Nigerian theatre because he established one of the first professional theatre companies in Nigeria and used drama to promote Nigerian culture and history.
2. Wole Soyinka - Wole Soyinka (born 1934) is a Nigerian playwright, poet, author, and professor. In 1986, he became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. His plays and writings promote justice, culture, and human rights.
3. Ola Rotimi - Ola Rotimi (1938-2000) was a Nigerian playwright and theatre director. He wrote many popular plays based on Nigerian history and culture, including The Gods Are Not to Blame. His works are widely studied in schools.
4. Zulu Sofola - Zulu Sofola (1935-1995) was a Nigerian playwright and educator. She was the first published female playwright in Nigeria. Her plays focused on African traditions, family life, and moral values.
5. Moses Olaiya - Moses Olaiya, popularly known as Baba Sala (1936-2018), was a Nigerian comedian, actor, playwright, and theatre producer. He became famous for his humorous stage plays and films and made significant contributions to the growth of Yoruba theatre and comedy.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF THEATRE PERSONNEL
Theatre personnel help to:
1. Produce successful stage performances.
2. Ensure every member performs his or her duty.
3. Make plays interesting and enjoyable.
4. Promote teamwork.
5. Preserve Nigerian culture through drama.
MATERIALS USED IN PLAY PRODUCTION
1. Drama script
2. Stage
3. Costumes
4. Props
5. Make-up materials
6. Lighting equipment
7. Microphones
8.  Speakers
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. A play production is the process of ______.
A. planting crops
B. preparing and presenting a drama
B. building a house
D. making furniture
2. Which of the following is an element of a play production?
A. Plate
B. Spoon
C. Script
D. Cup
3. Who directs and supervises actors during a play?
A. Carpenter
B. Doctor
C. Director
D. Tailor
4. Who watches a stage performance?
A. Costume designer
B. Producer
C. Stage manager
D. Audience
5. Which Nigerian theatre practitioner won the Nobel Prize in Literature?
A. Moses Olaiya
B. Hubert Ogunde
C. Ola Rotimi
D. Wole Soyinka
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: director, stage, costume, audience, script
6. The ______ is the written story of a play.
7. A play is performed on the ______.
8. The ______ supervises the actors.
9. The ______ watches the performance.
10. A ______ is the special clothing worn by actors.
C. True or False
11. Actors and actresses perform different roles in a play. ______
12. The producer organises and finances a play. ______
13. Hubert Ogunde is regarded as the father of Nigerian theatre. ______
14. Props are the people who watch a play. ______
15. Lighting helps the audience to see the actors clearly. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Producer - A. Supervises the actors
17. Director - B. Organises and finances the play
18. Stage Manager - C. Coordinates stage activities
19. Wole Soyinka - D. Nobel Prize-winning playwright
20. Hubert Ogunde - E. Father of Nigerian theatre
ANSWER KEYS
1. B - Preparing and presenting a drama
2. C- Script
3. C - Director
4. A - Audience
5. D - Wole Soyinka
6. script
7. stage
8. director
9. audience
10. costume
11. True
12. True
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. B - Organises and finances the play
17. A - Supervises the actors
18. C - Coordinates stage activities
19. D - Nobel Prize-winning playwright
20. E - Father of Nigerian theatre
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that a play production is the process of planning, preparing, and presenting a drama before an audience.
Pupils identified the elements of a play production, which include the script, actors and actresses, stage, costumes, props, lighting, sound and music, and audience. They also learned about the theatre personnel involved in a play production, such as the producer, director, stage manager, actors and actresses, costume designer, make-up artist, lighting technician, sound technician, and prop manager, together with their duties.
Furthermore, pupils learned about some notable Nigerian theatre practitioners, including Hubert Ogunde, Wole Soyinka, Ola Rotimi, Zulu Sofola, and Moses Olaiya (Baba Sala), and their contributions to the development of theatre and drama in Nigeria.
Finally, pupils understood that successful theatre productions require teamwork, proper planning, and the cooperation of all theatre personnel to entertain, educate, and preserve Nigerian culture.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays pictures of a stage performance or shows a short video of a drama. The teacher asks pupils to identify the people and materials involved in the performance before introducing the topic theatrical elements and personnel.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures or video and identify what they see.
Step 2: Elements of a Play Production - The teacher explains that a play production is the process of preparing and presenting a drama before an audience. The teacher also discusses the major elements of a play production:
- Script
- Actors and actresses
- Stage
- Costumes
- Props
- Lighting
- Sound and music
- Audience
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and explain the elements of a play production.
Step 3: Theatre Personnel and Their Duties - The teacher introduces the different theatre personnel and explains their duties:
- Producer
- Director
- Stage Manager
- Actor/Actress
- Costume Designer
- Make-up Artist
- Lighting Technician
- Sound Technician
- Prop Manager
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils match each theatre personnel with the correct duty.
Step 4: Notable Nigerian Theatre Practitioners - The teacher displays pictures of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners, including:
- Hubert Ogunde
- Wole Soyinka
- Ola Rotimi
- Zulu Sofola
- Moses Olaiya (Baba Sala)
The teacher gives a brief explanation of their contributions to Nigerian theatre.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the practitioners and mention one contribution made by each.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher assigns pupils different theatre roles such as producer, director, actor, stage manager, and costume designer for a short classroom drama.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils perform their assigned theatre roles during the activity.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: List the elements of a play production.
- Group 2: Identify the theatre personnel and explain their duties.
- Group 3: Discuss the contributions of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners.
- Group 4: Present a short role-play showing the cooperation of theatre personnel during a play production.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, role-play, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the elements of a play production, theatre personnel and their duties, and the contributions of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils during the group role-play.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate an understanding of the elements of a play production and the roles of theatre personnel.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Forms of Dance: Meaning, Types (Forms) of Dance, Notable Nigerian Dancers, and Dance Demonstration | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 4 Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of a play production.
2. Identify the elements of a play production.
3. Mention at least five theatre personnel and state their duties.
4. Identify at least three notable Nigerian theatre practitioners.
5. State the contributions of notable Nigerian theatre practitioners to the development of theatre in Nigeria.
6. Demonstrate teamwork by participating effectively in a simple classroom play production.

topics.title: Casting and Rehearsal: Meaning of Casting, Meaning of Rehearsal, Casting Process, and Planning a Rehearsal Schedule | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 8 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
CASTING AND REHEARSAL: MEANING OF CASTING AND REHEARSAL, CASTING PROCESS AND PLANNING A REHEARSAL SCHEDULE
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Choral Singing: Meaning, Classification (Types), and Importance of Choral Singing | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 6 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - CASTING AND REHEARSAL
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Cast and Casting Process
3. Meaning of Rehearsal and Rehearsal Schedule
4. Importance of Casting and Rehearsal and Materials Needed
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of casting.
2. Explain the meaning of rehearsal.
3. Describe the steps involved in the casting process.
4. Prepare a simple rehearsal schedule for a classroom play.
5. State the importance of casting and rehearsal in a drama production.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about drama and theatre, acting, theatrical elements and personnel, and character development.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing casting, rehearsal, the casting process, and planning a rehearsal schedule for a successful stage performance.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Drama script
2. Sample cast list
3. Sample rehearsal schedule
4. Flashcards showing drama characters
5. Costumes and stage props
6. Pictures or videos of drama rehearsals
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Before a drama is performed on stage, the actors and actresses must first be selected for different roles. They also need to practise many times so that they can perform confidently and avoid mistakes. This process of selecting performers is called casting, while the repeated practice before the final performance is called rehearsal.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of casting and rehearsal, the steps involved in the casting process, and how to plan a simple rehearsal schedule for a successful drama performance.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CASTING
Casting is the process of selecting suitable actors and actresses to play different roles in a drama or stage production.
CASTING PROCESS
The casting process usually involves the following steps:
1. Reading and understanding the script.
2. Identifying the different characters.
3. Auditioning interested actors and actresses.
4. Selecting the most suitable person for each role.
5. Assigning roles to the selected performers.
6. Informing the cast and preparing for rehearsals.
LESSON 2 - MEANING OF REHEARSAL
Rehearsal is the repeated practice of a play, song, or performance before it is presented to an audience. It helps performers improve their skills and confidence.
PLANNING A REHEARSAL SCHEDULE
A rehearsal schedule is a plan showing the dates, times, and activities for rehearsals.
A good rehearsal schedule should include:
1. Date of rehearsal.
2. Time of rehearsal.
3. Venue.
4. Scenes or activities to practise.
5. Names of the actors involved.
6. Materials or props needed.
SAMPLE REHEARSAL SCHEDULE
Day - Time - Activity
1. Monday - 2:00-3:00 p.m. - Script reading and role assignment
2. Wednesday - 2:00-3:30 p.m. - Practise scenes 1 and 2
3. Friday - 2:00-4:00 p.m. - Full rehearsal with costumes and props
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF CASTING AND REHEARSAL
Casting and rehearsal help to:
1. Select the best performers for each role.
2. Improve acting and speaking skills.
3. Build confidence among performers.
4. Correct mistakes before the final performance.
5. Promote teamwork and cooperation.
6. Ensure a successful stage performance.
MATERIALS NEEDED
1. Drama script
2. Costumes
3. Props
4. Stage
5. Chairs
6. Rehearsal timetable
7. Writing materials
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Casting is the process of _______.
A. painting the stage
B. selecting actors and actresses for different roles
C. writing songs
D. designing costumes
2. Rehearsal is the _______ before the final performance.
A. repeated practice
B. payment of actors
C. decoration of the hall
D. repeated practice
3. Which of the following comes first in the casting process?
A. Decorating the stage
B. Performing before the audience
C. Buying costumes
D. Reading and understanding the script
4. A rehearsal schedule helps actors to know the _______.
A. weather B. ticket price
C. rehearsal dates, time, and activities
D. audience names
5. Which of the following is an importance of rehearsal?
A. It improves performance.
B. It delays the performance.
C. It reduces teamwork.
D. It prevents acting.
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: casting, actors, rehearsal, schedule, script
6. _______ is the process of selecting performers for different roles.
7. A _______ is the repeated practice before a performance.
8. The drama _______ contains the story and dialogue.
9. A rehearsal _______ shows the date, time, and activities for practice.
10. The selected _______ perform the different roles in a play.
C. True or False
11. Casting helps to select suitable actors and actresses. _______
12. Rehearsal is done after the final performance. _______
13. A rehearsal schedule helps to organise practice sessions. _______
14. Teamwork is important during rehearsal. _______
15. Rehearsal helps actors become more afraid. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Casting - A. Plan showing rehearsal dates and activities
17. Rehearsal - B. Selecting actors for different roles
18. Script - C. Written story of a play
19. Rehearsal Schedule - D. Repeated practice before performance
20. Actor - E. Performs a role in a play
ANSWER KEYS
1. B - Selecting actors and actresses for different roles
2. D - Repeated practice
3. D - Reading and understanding the script
4. C - Rehearsal dates, time, and activities
5. A - It improves performance.
6. casting
7. rehearsal
8. script
9. schedule
10. actors
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. True
15. False
16. B - Selecting actors for different roles
17. D - Repeated practice before performance
18. C - Written story of a play
19. A - Plan showing rehearsal dates and activities
20. E - Performs a role in a Play
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that casting is the process of selecting suitable actors and actresses to play different roles in a drama, while rehearsal is the repeated practice of a play before it is presented to an audience.
Pupils learned the steps involved in the casting process, which include reading the script, identifying the characters, conducting auditions, selecting suitable performers, assigning roles, and preparing for rehearsals.
They also learned how to plan a rehearsal schedule by including the date, time, venue, scenes to be practised, participants, and materials needed for each rehearsal session.
Finally, pupils understood that casting and rehearsal are important because they help to select the best performers, improve acting skills, build confidence, correct mistakes, encourage teamwork, and ensure a successful drama performance.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays a drama script and asks pupils how actors are chosen for different roles before a play is performed. The teacher introduces the topic Casting and Rehearsal.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the script and discuss how actors are selected and prepared for a play.
Step 2: Meaning of Casting and Rehearsal - The teacher explains that:
- Casting is the process of selecting suitable actors and actresses for different roles in a play.
- Rehearsal is the repeated practice of a play before the final performance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meanings of casting and rehearsal in their own words.
Step 3: Casting Process - The teacher explains the steps involved in casting:
- Reading and understanding the script
- Identifying the characters
- Conducting auditions
- Selecting suitable actors and actresses
- Assigning roles
- Preparing for rehearsals
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils arrange the casting steps in the correct order.
Step 4: Planning a Rehearsal Schedule - The teacher displays a sample rehearsal schedule and explains its components:
- Date
- Time
- Venue
- Scenes or activities to practise
- Actors involved
- Materials or props needed
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils prepare a simple rehearsal schedule for a classroom drama.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher conducts a simple classroom audition by assigning different roles to willing pupils and guiding them through a short rehearsal.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils participate in the audition, accept assigned roles, and rehearse a short scene.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of casting and rehearsal.
- Group 2: List and explain the steps in the casting process.
- Group 3: Prepare a simple rehearsal schedule for a classroom play.
- Group 4: Present a short rehearsal of a selected scene using the assigned roles.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, plan, rehearse, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meanings of casting and rehearsal, the casting process, the rehearsal schedule, and the importance of proper preparation before a stage performance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils’ participation during the casting and rehearsal activities.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate an understanding of casting, rehearsal, and rehearsal planning through their classroom performance.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of casting.
2. Explain the meaning of rehearsal.
3. State five steps involved in the casting process.
3. Prepare a simple rehearsal schedule showing the date, time, venue, and activities.
4. State at least five importance of casting and rehearsal.
5. Participate actively in a simple classroom rehearsal by performing an assigned role confidently and cooperatively.

topics.title: Choral Singing: Meaning, Classification (Types), and Importance of Choral Singing | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 6 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
CHORAL SINGING: MEANING, CLASSIFICATION (TYPES) AND IMPORTANCE OF CHORAL SINGING
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 6
THEME -  MUSIC
PREVIOUS LESSON - Imaginative and Creative Drawing: Meaning, Characteristics, Drawing from Imagination, and Evaluating Artwork | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 5 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - CHORAL SINGING
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Classification (Types) of Choral Singing
3. Importance of Choral Singing
4. Qualities of a Good Choir
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of choral singing.
2. Identify the different types of choral singing.
3. State the importance of choral singing.
4. Describe the qualities of a good choir.
5. Participate confidently in a simple choral singing performance.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about rhythmic patterns, music notes and their values, forms of dance, and singing simple songs.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing choral singing, its types, and its importance in music and society.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Songbook or hymnbook
2. Music sheets
3. Keyboard or piano (if available)
4. Drums or percussion instruments
5. Audio recordings of choir performances
6. Pictures or videos of different choirs
7. Microphone (if available)
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Many songs are more enjoyable when people sing together as a group. In schools, churches, and special events, groups of singers called choirs perform songs under the direction of a choir conductor. Choral singing requires teamwork, discipline, correct rhythm, and harmony.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of choral singing, the different types of choirs, the importance of choral singing, and participate in a simple group singing activity.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF CHORAL SINGING
Choral singing is the performance of songs by a group of singers who sing together under the guidance of a choir director or conductor.
CLASSIFICATION (TYPES) OF CHORAL SINGING
Choral singing can be classified into:
1. Children’s Choir - A choir made up of children.
2. Male Choir - A choir consisting only of male singers.
3. Female Choir - A choir consisting only of female singers.
4. Mixed Choir - A choir made up of both male and female singers.
5. School Choir - A choir organised in schools for pupils and students.
6. Church Choir - A choir that sings during religious services.
MATERIALS NEEDED FOR CHORAL SINGING
1. Songbook or hymnbook
2. Music sheets
3. Keyboard or piano
4. Drums or percussion instruments
5. Microphones (if available)
6. Choir uniforms or robes (optional)
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF CHORAL SINGING
Choral singing helps to:
1. Promote teamwork and cooperation.
2. Develop good singing skills.
3. Improve confidence when performing.
4. Encourage discipline and obedience.
5. Preserve cultural and religious songs.
6. Provide entertainment.
7. Improve listening and communication skills.
QUALITIES OF A GOOD CHOIR
A good choir should:
1. Sing with one voice and proper harmony.
2. Follow the conductor’s instructions.
3. Maintain correct posture while singing.
4. Pronounce words clearly.
5. Keep to the correct rhythm and tempo.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Choral singing is performed by ______.
A. one singer only
B. a group of singers
C. a drummer only
D. a dancer only
2. A person who directs a choir is called a ______.
A. conductor
B. referee
C. painter
D. farmer
3. Which of the following is a type of choir?
A. Market choir
B. Football choir
C. School choir
D. Kitchen choir
4. Which choir consists of both male and female singers?
A. Children’s choir
B. Male choir
C. Female choir
D. Mixed choir
5. Choral singing helps to promote ______.
A. carelessness
B. laziness
C. quarrelling
D. teamwork
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: choir, school, conductor, teamwork, harmony
6. Choral singing is performed by a ______.
7. A choir is led by a ______.
8. Good choir members sing in ______.
9. A ______ choir is organised in schools.
10. Choral singing encourages ______.
C. True or False
11. Choral singing is performed by only one person. ______
12. A mixed choir consists of only male or female singers. ______
13. Choral singing helps to build confidence. ______
14. Choir members should follow the conductor’s instructions. ______
15. Choral singing damage listening skills. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Children’s choir - A. Singing together pleasantly
17. Mixed choir - B. Choir made up of children
18. Conductor - C. Choir organised in a school
19. Harmony - D. Male and female singers
20. School choir - E. Leads the choir
ANSWER KEYS
1. B - A group of singers
2. A - Conductor
3. C - School choir
4. D - Mixed choir
5. D - Teamwork
6. choir
7. conductor
8. harmony
9. school
10. teamwork
11. False
12. Fals
13. True
14. True
15. False
16. B - Choir made up of children
17. D - Male and female singers
18. E - Leads the choir
19. A - Singing together pleasantly
20. C - Choir organised in a school
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that choral singing is the performance of songs by a group of singers under the direction of a choir conductor.
Pupils identified the different types of choral singing, including children’s choir, male choir, female choir, mixed choir, school choir, and church choir. They also learned the qualities of a good choir, such as singing in harmony, maintaining correct posture, following the conductor’s instructions, pronouncing words clearly, and keeping to the correct rhythm and tempo.
Furthermore, pupils learned the importance of choral singing, including promoting teamwork, discipline, confidence, musical skills, communication, cultural preservation, and entertainment.
Finally, pupils participated in a simple choral singing activity, where they practised singing together in harmony while following the guidance of the choir conductor.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher plays a recording of a choir or leads the class in singing a familiar song together. The teacher asks pupils how singing together differs from singing alone before introducing the topic Choral Singing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen, sing along, and respond to the teacher’s questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Choral Singing - The teacher explains that choral singing is the performance of songs by a group of singers under the direction of a choir conductor.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of choral singing in their own words.
Step 3: Types of Choral Singing - The teacher explains the different types of choral singing:
- Children’s choir
- Male choir
- Female choir
- Mixed choir
- School choir
- Church choir
The teacher displays pictures or videos of each type.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the different types of choirs and describe them.
Step 4: Importance of Choral Singing - The teacher discusses the importance of choral singing, including:
- Promotes teamwork and cooperation.
- Develops singing skills.
- Builds confidence.
- Encourages discipline.
- Preserves cultural and religious songs.
- Provides entertainment.
- Improves listening and communication skills.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain why choral singing is important.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher arranges the pupils into a simple choir and teaches them a short song. The teacher demonstrates how to stand correctly, watch the conductor, and sing in harmony.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils sing together while following the teacher’s directions.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of choral singing.
- Group 2: Identify and describe the different types of choral singing.
- Group 3: State the importance of choral singing.
- Group 4: Perform a simple choral song while following the instructions of a group conductor.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, sing, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning, types, qualities, and importance of choral singing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils as they participate in the group singing activity.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate proper choral singing by singing in harmony, maintaining good posture, and following the conductor’s instructions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Casting and Rehearsal: Meaning of Casting, Meaning of Rehearsal, Casting Process, and Planning a Rehearsal Schedule | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 8 Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Explain the meaning of choral singing.
2. Identify at least five types of choral singing.
3. State at least five importance of choral singing.
4. Describe the qualities of a good choir.
5. Demonstrate proper choral singing by singing in harmony, maintaining good posture, and following the conductor’s instructions.
6. Participate actively and confidently in a group choral singing performance.

topics.title: Imaginative and Creative Drawing: Meaning, Characteristics, Drawing from Imagination, and Evaluating Artwork | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 5 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING: MEANING, CHARACTERISTICS, DRAWING FROM IMAGINATION AND EVALUATING ARTWORK
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 5
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Forms of Dance: Meaning, Types (Forms) of Dance, Notable Nigerian Dancers, and Dance Demonstration | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 4 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Characteristics of Imaginative and Creative Drawing
3. Materials used in Drawing and Drawing from Imagination
4. Meaning and Importance of Evaluating Artwork
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of imaginative drawing.
2. Explain the meaning of creative drawing.
3. State the characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing.
4. Produce a simple drawing from imagination.
5. Evaluate an artwork using appropriate criteria such as neatness, creativity, originality, and colour combination.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about life drawing, drawing simple objects, shading, and colouring techniques.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing imaginative and creative drawing, where pupils create original artworks from their own ideas and imagination.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencils
3. Erasers
4. Sharpeners
5. Crayons
7. Colour pencils
8. Markers
9. Sample imaginative and creative drawings
10. Charts showing drawing techniques
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Have you ever imagined a place, an animal, or a machine that does not exist and wished to draw it? Artists often create pictures from their imagination instead of copying what they see. Such drawings allow them to express their ideas, feelings, and creativity in unique ways.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning and characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing, practise drawing from imagination, and learn how to evaluate artworks based on creativity, neatness, originality, and overall appearance.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING
Imaginative drawing is drawing pictures from one’s ideas, thoughts, or imagination without directly copying an object.
Creative drawing is producing original drawings by using imagination, creativity, and artistic skills to express ideas and feelings.
CHARACTERISTICS OF IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING
Imaginative and creative drawings:
1. Are original and unique.
2. Express ideas and feelings.
3. Show creativity and imagination.
4. May include real or imaginary objects.
5. Use colours, shapes, and patterns creatively.
6. Reflect the artist’s personal style.
MATERIALS FOR IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencil
3. Eraser
4. Sharpener
5. Crayons
6. Colour pencils
7. Markers
8. Ruler (if needed)
LESSON 2 - DRAWING FROM IMAGINATION
Drawing from imagination involves:
1. Thinking of an idea or theme.
2. Visualising the picture in the mind.
3. Sketching the main objects lightly.
4. Adding details to the drawing.
5. Colouring the artwork neatly.
6. Giving the drawing a suitable title.
EVALUATING ARTWORK
Evaluating artwork means examining a drawing to identify its strengths and areas for improvement.
When evaluating artwork, consider:
1. Neatness
2. Creativity
3. Correct use of colours
4. Balance and arrangement
5. Originality
6. Overall appearance
IMPORTANCE OF IMAGINATIVE AND CREATIVE DRAWING
It helps pupils to:
1. Develop creativity.
2. Improve imagination.
3. Build self-confidence.
4. Express thoughts and emotions.
5. Improve observation and drawing skills.
6. Appreciate works of art.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Imaginative drawing is drawing from one’s ________.
A. imagination
B. textbook
C. photograph only
D. computer screen
2. Creative drawing helps an artist to express ________.
A. numbers
B. hunger
C. homework only
D. ideas and feelings
3. Which of the following is a characteristic of imaginative drawing?
A. Noise
B. Laziness
C. Originality
D. Carelessness
4. Which of the following is used for colouring a drawing?
A. Spoon
B. Crayon
C. Plate
D. Cup
5. Which of the following should be considered when evaluating artwork?
A. Neatness
B. Shoe size
C. Height of the artist
D. Age of the artist
B. Fill in the Gaps
Complete the sentences using the words in the box: imagination, originality, colours, artwork, pencil
6. Imaginative drawing comes from the artist’s ______.
7. A ______ is commonly used for sketching.
8. Good ______ make a drawing attractive.
9. Every creative drawing should show ______.
10. A completed drawing is called an ______.
C. True or False
11. Creative drawing allows artists to express their ideas. ______
12. Imaginative drawing must always copy a real object. ______
13. Neatness is important when evaluating artwork. ______
14. Colour combination can reduce the quality of a drawing. ______
15. Originality is one quality of creative drawing. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Imagination - A. Freedom to create ideas
17. Pencil - B. Judging the quality of artwork
18. Colour - C. Quality of a good artwork
19. Neatness - D. Used for sketching
20. Evaluation - E. Makes artwork attractive
ANSWER KEYS
1. A - Imagination
2. D - Ideas and feelings
3. C - Originality
4. B - Crayon
5. A - Neatness
6. imagination
7. pencil
8. colours
9. originality
10. artwork
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. A - Freedom to create ideas
17. D - Used for sketching
18. E - Makes artwork attractive
19. C - Quality of a good artwork
20. B - Judging the quality of artwork
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that imaginative drawing is drawing from one’s ideas, thoughts, or imagination without directly copying an object, while creative drawing is producing original artworks that express ideas and feelings.
Pupils identified the characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing, including originality, creativity, imagination, neatness, proper use of colours, and personal expression. They also learned the steps involved in drawing from imagination, such as thinking of an idea, sketching, adding details, colouring neatly, and giving the artwork a suitable title.
Furthermore, pupils learned how to evaluate artwork by considering qualities such as neatness, creativity, originality, colour combination, balance, and overall appearance.
Finally, pupils practised creating their own imaginative drawings and developed an appreciation for creativity, self-expression, and artistic excellence through artwork evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays different imaginative and creative drawings and asks pupils what they observe. The teacher encourages pupils to describe the pictures and explain whether they were copied from real objects or created from imagination.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the drawings, describe what they see, and share their opinions.
Step 2: Meaning of Imaginative and Creative Drawing - The teacher explains that imaginative drawing is drawing from one’s ideas or imagination, while creative drawing is producing original artwork that expresses ideas and feelings.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meanings of imaginative and creative drawing in their own words.
Step 3: Characteristics of Imaginative and Creative Drawing - The teacher discusses the characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing, including:
- Originality
- Creativity
- Imagination
- Neatness
- Proper use of colours
- Personal expression
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the characteristics shown in sample drawings.
Step 4: Drawing from Imagination - The teacher demonstrates how to create a drawing from imagination by:
- Thinking of an idea or theme.
- Sketching the main objects lightly.
- Adding details.
- Colouring the drawing neatly.
- Giving the artwork a suitable title.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils create their own imaginative drawings by following the demonstration.
Step 5: Evaluating Artwork - The teacher explains how artwork can be evaluated using the following criteria:
- Neatness
- Creativity
- Originality
- Colour combination
- Balance and arrangement
- Overall appearance
The teacher guides pupils to assess sample artworks.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils evaluate drawings using the given criteria and give simple reasons for their opinions.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of imaginative and creative drawing.
- Group 2: List the characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing.
- Group 3: Produce a simple drawing from imagination.
- Group 4: Evaluate the drawings produced by other groups using the agreed criteria.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, draw, evaluate, and present their assigned activities.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meanings of imaginative and creative drawing, their characteristics, the steps for drawing from imagination, and the criteria for evaluating artwork.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and assesses pupils’ imaginative drawings based on originality, creativity, neatness, colour use, and overall presentation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and submit their drawings for assessment.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Choral Singing: Meaning, Classification (Types), and Importance of Choral Singing | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 6 Cultural and Creative Arts
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of imaginative drawing.
2. Explain the meaning of creative drawing.
3. State at least five characteristics of imaginative and creative drawing.
4. Produce a simple drawing from imagination.
5. Evaluate an artwork using criteria such as neatness, creativity, originality, colour combination, balance, and overall appearance.
6. Appreciate and respect the creative ideas expressed in their own artworks and those of others.

topics.title: Introduction to Still Life Drawing: Meaning of Still Life Drawing and Drawing the Human Figure | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 9 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
INTRODUCTION TO STILL LIFE DRAWING: MEANING OF STILL LIFE DRAWING AND DRAWING HUMAN FIGURE
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS (CCA)
PRIMARY 6 - SECOND TERM - WEEK 9
THEME -  ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Recycling: Meaning, Importance, Materials That Can Be Recycled and Recycling Plastic Bottles for Useful Purposes | Primary 6 (Basic 6) Second Term Week 8 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - STILL LIFE DRAWING
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Characteristics of Still Life Drawing
3. Meaning Drawing the Human Figure and Steps Drawing Human Figure
4. Importance of Still Life and Human Figure Drawing and Materials Needed
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of still life drawing.
2. Identify common objects used for still life drawing.
3. State the characteristics of a good still life drawing.
4. Explain the meaning of human figure drawing.
5. Draw a simple still life arrangement.
6. Draw a simple human figure showing the major body parts.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about imaginative and creative drawing, life drawing, and the use of drawing materials such as pencils, erasers, and drawing paper.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing still life drawing and human figure drawing, using careful observation and simple sketching techniques.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencils
3. Erasers
4. Sharpeners
5. Rulers
6. Colour pencils or crayons
7. A still life arrangement (e.g., bottle, cup, fruit, flower vase, basket, books)
8. Charts or pictures of human figures
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every day, we see many objects around us such as bottles, cups, fruits, books, and flower vases. Artists carefully observe these objects and draw them just as they appear. This type of drawing is called still life drawing. Artists also draw people to show their appearance, posture, and movement. This is known as human figure drawing.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of still life drawing, identify objects used in still life drawing, understand the meaning of human figure drawing, and practise drawing simple still life objects and a human figure.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF STILL LIFE DRAWING
Still life drawing is the art of drawing non-living objects that are arranged in one place. These objects remain still while the artist observes and draws them.
Examples of objects used for still life drawing include:
- Fruits
- Flower vase
- Bottle
- Cup
- Plate
- Basket
- Books
- Shoes
CHARACTERISTICS OF STILL LIFE DRAWING
A good still life drawing should:
1. Show the correct shape of the objects.
2. Have proper proportion and size.
3. Be neatly arranged.
4. Show light and shade where necessary.
5. Be neat and attractive.
LESSON 2 - MEANING OF HUMAN FIGURE DRAWING
Human figure drawing is the drawing of the whole human body or parts of the body such as the head, hands, legs, or face.
It helps artists understand the shape, size, posture, and movement of the human body.
STEPS IN DRAWING THE HUMAN FIGURE
1. Draw simple guidelines using light lines.
2. Sketch the head.
3. Draw the neck and body.
4. Add the arms and hands.
5. Draw the legs and feet.
6. Add facial features such as the eyes, nose, ears, and mouth.
7. Draw clothing if necessary.
8. Erase unnecessary lines and colour or shade the drawing.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF STILL LIFE AND HUMAN FIGURE DRAWING
Still life and human figure drawing help learners to:
1. Develop observation skills.
2. Improve drawing skills.
3. Develop creativity.
4. Understand proportion and balance.
5. Appreciate beauty in art.
6. Build patience and concentration.
MATERIALS NEEDED
1. Drawing paper
2. Pencil
3. Eraser
4. Sharpener
5. Ruler
6. Colour pencils or crayons
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Still life drawing is the drawing of ________.
A. wild animals
B. moving vehicles
C. non-living objects
D. rivers
2. Which of the following can be used for still life drawing?
A. Bottle
B. Bird flying
C. Running child
D. Swimming fish
3. Human figure drawing is the drawing of the ________.
A. market
B. classroom
C. human body
D. playground
4. Which material is commonly used for drawing?
A. Bucket
B. Spoon
C. Plate
D. Pencil
5. A good still life drawing should have correct ________.
A. Speech
B. proportion
C. speed
D. temperature
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: paper, objects, observation, body, shading
6. Still life drawing involves drawing non-living _______.
7. Human figure drawing shows the human _______.
8. Artists use careful _______ before drawing.
9. _______ makes a drawing look more realistic.
10. Drawings are usually made on drawing _______.
C. True or False
11. Fruits can be used in life drawing. _______
12. Human figure drawing helps artists understand body proportion. _______
13. A still life arrangement contains moving objects. _______
14. A pencil is a drawing material. _______
15. Still life drawing decreases observation skills. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that still life drawing is the drawing of non-living objects arranged in one place for observation and sketching. They identified common still life objects such as bottles, fruits, flower vases, cups, plates, baskets, books, and shoes.
Pupils also learned the characteristics of a good still life drawing, which include correct shape, proper proportion, neat arrangement, appropriate shading, and neatness.
Furthermore, pupils learned that human figure drawing is the drawing of the whole human body or its parts. They studied the basic steps involved in drawing the human figure, including sketching the head, body, arms, legs, facial features, and clothing.
Finally, pupils understood that still life drawing and human figure drawing help to develop observation skills, creativity, patience, concentration, and the ability to draw objects and people with correct proportion and balance.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher displays a simple still life arrangement containing objects such as a bottle, fruit, cup, and flower vase. The teacher asks pupils to identify the objects and observe their shapes before introducing the topic Introduction to Still Life Drawing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the objects and describe their shapes, sizes, and positions.
Step 2: Meaning of Still Life Drawing - The teacher explains that still life drawing is the drawing of non-living objects arranged in one place for observation and Sketching. Also, the teacher gives examples of objects used in still life drawing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of still life drawing and identify still life objects around them.
Step 3: Characteristics of a Good Still Life Drawing - The teacher explains that a good still life drawing should have:
- Correct shape
- Proper proportion
- Neat arrangement
- Appropriate shading
- Neat finishing
Also, the teacher demonstrates using a simple sketch.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the demonstration and identify the characteristics in the sample drawing.
Step 4: Meaning of Human Figure Drawing - The teacher explains that human figure drawing is the drawing of the whole human body or its parts. Also, the teacher displays a chart showing the basic parts of the human body.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the major parts of the human body used in drawing.
Step 5: Practical Demonstration - The teacher demonstrates how to draw a simple human figure by:
- Drawing light guidelines.
- Sketching the head.
- Drawing the neck and body.
- Adding the arms and hands.
- Drawing the legs and feet.
- Adding facial features and clothing.
- Erasing unnecessary lines and shading where necessary.
The teacher also demonstrates a simple still life drawing.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils draw a simple still life arrangement and a human figure by following the teacher’s demonstration.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following activities:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of still life drawing.
- Group 2: Identify objects used in still life drawing.
- Group 3: Draw a simple still life arrangement.
- Group 4: Draw a simple human figure and label the major body parts.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, draw, observe, and present their work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the meaning of still life drawing, the characteristics of a good still life drawing, the meaning of human figure drawing, and the basic steps involved in drawing a human figure.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and assesses pupils’ drawings.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate their understanding by producing neat still life drawings and simple human figure sketches with correct proportion and observation.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
